semantic_correction.stem: A client recently diagnosed with HIV says, 'I do not know how I will manage this for the rest of my life.' Which nursing plan best supports long-term adjustment?

options.A: Use ongoing nonjudgmental conversations to identify changing emotional, adherence, social, and structural needs and connect the client with appropriate support services.
options.B: Concentrate follow-up on medication-taking and viral-load results, and discuss mental health, stigma, relationships, or practical barriers only if adherence later declines.
options.C: Provide a comprehensive psychosocial discussion at diagnosis, then limit later visits to treatment monitoring because most adjustment needs should resolve once ART begins.
options.D: Assume that achieving viral suppression means psychosocial adaptation is complete, and reserve navigation, case-management, or peer-support referrals for treatment failure.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. CDC's Clinical Care of HIV guidance, updated April 16, 2026, recommends regular conversations at every office visit to identify adherence barriers, offer support services, and uncover changing challenges to staying in care. CDC identifies psychosocial barriers such as mental-health concerns, substance use, negative beliefs about HIV, low quality of life, and lack of social support, and recommends referral when appropriate to patient navigators, psychologists, addiction specialists, support groups, adherence counselors, and case managers. It also identifies structural barriers such as transportation, housing, childcare, and insurance and recommends navigation and support for these needs. CDC further states that brief conversations at each office visit help uncover barriers to successful long-term treatment and facilitate access to services and resources as needs change over time. B is incorrect because HIV care should not be reduced to medication and laboratory monitoring or wait for adherence failure before psychosocial barriers are addressed. C is incorrect because support needs can change over time and should be reassessed beyond the initial diagnosis visit. D is incorrect because viral suppression is a treatment goal but does not eliminate the need for ongoing assessment of psychosocial, structural, and retention-in-care needs.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Support long-term HIV adjustment through recurring, nonjudgmental assessment of emotional, adherence, social, and structural needs and connection to appropriate mental-health, navigation, case-management, peer, and community resources as needs evolve.

semantic_correction.source_locator: Clinical Care of HIV → Help your patients adhere to ART by engaging in regular conversations at every office visit: identify barriers, offer adherence-support services, use open-ended questions. Psychosocial barriers: mental-health issues, substance use, negative HIV beliefs, low quality of life, and lack of social support; refer to patient navigators, psychologists, addiction specialists, support groups, adherence counselors, and case managers. Structural barriers: transportation, housing, childcare, and insurance; connect with navigators/support. Keeping patients in care → build positive relationships, address barriers, actively refer to relevant services, and engage in brief conversations at every office visit so services/resources can change as needs evolve.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports recurring, nonjudgmental assessment of adherence, psychosocial, and structural barriers throughout HIV care and active connection to navigation, mental-health, case-management, peer/support-group, and other services as needs change over time.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the absolute-word and answer-length cues, rebuilt all four care plans to near-equal length, freshly verified April 2026 CDC HIV clinical-care guidance, and strengthened the item to test recurring assessment and evolving support needs rather than a one-time or medication-only model.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests ongoing individualized psychosocial support in long-term HIV care with one clearly best plan, balanced alternatives, current federal guidance, and no absolute-word or answer-length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches CDC guidance for recurring nonjudgmental conversations, identification of changing barriers, and connection to appropriate support services throughout care.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC recommends addressing psychosocial and structural barriers proactively, not only after medication adherence declines.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. HIV-related needs can evolve over time; CDC recommends brief conversations and barrier assessment at every office visit rather than only at diagnosis.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Viral suppression does not erase mental-health, social, structural, or retention needs and is not a reason to stop psychosocial assessment or referrals.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely combines ongoing reassessment with evolving service linkage; B defers psychosocial care until adherence worsens, C restricts support to diagnosis, and D incorrectly equates viral suppression with complete psychosocial adaptation.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel longitudinal care plans of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'only' distractor and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
